docs.title: Panoptes
docs.text:
-> PANOPTES (Panoptic Astronomical Networked Observatories for a Public Transiting Exoplanets Survey) is a citizen science project that aims to deploy compact robotic telescopes designed for continuous, high-precision photometry—measuring characteristics like light intensity and color.

-> My role in this is as a speecialist in benchbuilding, where we train ourselves to repair or assemble a PANOPTES Unit without incurring the costs of either building a new unit or of taking apart an existing unit.

Additionally, I also have some experience in Image Stacking using software such as Siril, as well as in the usage of Stellarium in order to find and target stars for viewing using the PANOPTES Units.

docs.title: Siril
docs.text:
-> Siril is an image tool which can stack images, analyze images, and do much more (more details on their website).

It can take multiple modules to do many kinds of tasks, with the most important in our application being Starnet, which allows us to stack images automatically using a Python script

This documentation is meant to help set up Siril, to show the installation of Starnet, and how the images must be set up in order to stack them.

docs.title: Installation of Siril
docs.text:
First of all, we go to the website, where we are greeted by the following screen:

Here, we can select the OS we are running and select the installer depending on OS and the chip (in case of Mac). However, since I am using a Windows, I will be selecting the Windows option. To make installation and running easier for Windows users, I recommend using the Portable installer, which installs a zip file with an .exe file in the bin folder.

Run the siril.exe file, let the Windows CMD do some background processes, and you will see this screen.

docs.title: The Setup & Process
docs.text:
-> Now you must press the blue button for a drop-down menu like this, and press 'Get Scripts' to get a menu as shown below:

Now search up mono_preprocessing_withoutDBF and enable it since this is the main script that stacks our images.

Nest, press the home button (coloured blue) and set up a directory with a folder named 'lights', where you will be keeping the images that you want to stack (images are in .fits).

Then you set the working directory as the parent folder for the images folder, which in my case here would be 'Pictures'. Go to that folder and press 'Open' (located at bottom-right of the window).

Then you can go back to the drop-down menu, script list, and click on the script that we installed (mono_preprocessing_withoutDBF).

Let the script run its course, and it will finish stacking it for you, with the time taken depending on the number of images to stack.

When done, there should be a new file called 'result.fits' in the parent folder for the images, which you can open to see the result of the script.

(Do remember to set this particular setting from 'Linear' to 'Autostretch'):

Now we shall take a detour to install Starnet, which is a script or software that helps in removing stars from the image, as far as my own knowledge goes for this app. In this case, it will help us to see only the galaxy in the image shown, so as to observe it better.

Firstly, we go to the Starnet download page where we will install a .exe file or zip file according to preference and OS.

I have not used the installer, but instead used the zip file. so this documentation is mainly for the installation of the zip file.

After installing the zip file, we extract it and leave it anywhere, as long as you do not forget where it is.

Then, go press the three bars near the minimize button at the top-right, press preferences and see this screen:

Go to 'Miscellaneous' and after pressing the first option to select a file from the 'Software Location' menu, select the starnet2.exe file in your unzipped folder.

After this, there should be the 'Image Processing' menu above in the options.

Press on that for a drop-down menu, select 'Star Processing', then 'Starnet Star Removal'. You will see a menu with options for star removal, where you can tweak it if you must and press 'Execute'. In our case, we can leave it as default.

Then we will get an image without stars as seen below:

With this result (possibly) being on your screen, you can rest assured that you know how to do this now.

docs.title: Stellarium
docs.text:
-> It is a free software that allows users to view the sky at various times of day from different locations.

It is easily modifiable, with possibilities of helping to visualize the view of a certain section of the sky from different telescopes and eyepieces, as well as visualizing the visibility of stars in the night sky with different levels of light pollution.

This document, apart from giving an idea on what it is capable of, is also for the purpose of giving an idea on what the most commonly used tools in Space and Tech as a whole are used for, and how you can use them.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
-> The installation process is very straightforward, as you directly go to the official Stellarium website (link here), select your OS, and install the zip file or installer depending on the content. After that, you either have to extract the files from the zip file, or run the installer and follow the instructions in order to install Stellarium in your computer.

-> If, for any reason, you cannot install Stellarium, you can use the web variant, but as far as my experience goes, there is not much functionality, being limited to the current time and location, with the only good thing being able to see what planets are up at night, and at what times. A view of the web variant is below:

docs.title: Usage of Tools
docs.text:
-> The moment we open up Stellarium, we are graced by the following screen: Now, if we were to move the cursor to the left side of the screen around the near-bottom (as shown in the bottom image). we will be greeted by the following tools: The tools available here from top to bottom are: 1. Location setting 2. Time setting 3. Sky viewing options 4. Search 5. Configuration 6. Astronomical Calculator 7. Help Out of these tools, we usually use settings 1-5 since it helps set a location, plan a time for stargazing, see the effects of light pollution, search up stars, and configure your settings as required.

There are also more tools that can be accessed if the cursor is moved to the bottom, where we can select which celestial objects are visible in the app, helping narrow down the stars that you want to see, and also helping your computer to run smoothly.

docs.title: A deeper look at tools 1 and 2
Location setting
docs.text: -> This tool, as the name suggests, lets you set the location of the observer in the application so that you can visualize the sky at that particular location.

docs.title: Time setting
docs.text: -> This tool lets you set the time and day according to either the standard date and time system or the Julian Day, depending on which one is being shown in your information.

docs.title: Finding RA and Dec
docs.text:
-> In PANOPTES or Space and Tech in general, we use the RA and Dec values to find the location of a certain object in the sky. The values serve as coordinates, and are used by telescopes, Stellarium, equatorial mounts like the ones used for PANOPTES Units, and other applications. To find the values, you simply have to click on the celestial object you want to find the values for, and find the appropriate numbers on the left side where information is displayed. Then you convert the values to a preferred unit, and then you can use it in the applications that were detailed above.

-> This concludes the usage of Stellarium from my side, and I urge exploration for other options as I myself did not finish exploring all options.

Adding a New Project

  1. Copy project-template.md and rename it (e.g., smart-home-system.md)

  2. Fill in your project details using the template structure

  3. Add a card above by copying a project card block

  4. Update mkdocs.yml — add your new page:

    nav:
  - Projects:
      - Overview: projects/index.md
      - "📋 Project Template": projects/project-template.md
      - Smart Home System: projects/smart-home-system.md  # ← add here

  5. Run mkdocs serve and check it out!
